title: Spectroscopy using dipole-phonon quantum logic
authors: Lu Qi, Evan C. Reed, Duanyang Wang, Boyan Yu, Kenneth R. Brown
abstract: Dipole-phonon quantum logic (DPQL) offers novel approaches for state preparation, measurement, and control of quantum information in molecular ion qubits. Here we report the first experimental demonstration of DPQL as a spectroscopic tool using the shared motional mode of a CaO$^+$-Ca$^+$ ion chain to measure the frequency splitting of the ground $Ω$-doublet of CaO$^+$. By comparing the dipole-phonon signal across three trap-frequency ramp ranges, we determine the splitting to be $ω_{mol}=2π\times454\pm1$ kHz and place a lower bound on the effective dipole-phonon coupling. The rate of observation is limited by the low thermal population in the molecular ground rotational state.
summary: This paper reports the first experimental use of Dipole-Phonon Quantum Logic (DPQL) spectroscopy on $	ext{CaO}^+$ ions to measure the frequency splitting of its ground state. By analyzing signal patterns across multiple motional frequency ramps, the authors determined the splitting to be $2\pi 	imes 454 \pm 1$ kHz. The methodology combines advanced trapped-ion cooling techniques with sophisticated statistical analysis to achieve high-precision quantum characterization.
main_problem: The primary goal was to demonstrate Dipole-Phonon Quantum Logic (DPQL) as a novel spectroscopic tool to precisely measure the frequency splitting ($\omega_{	ext{mol}}$) of the ground $\Omega$-doublet of the $	ext{CaO}^+$ molecular ion.
main_result: The experiment successfully measured the molecular splitting frequency to be $\omega_{	ext{mol}} = 2\pi 	imes 454 \pm 1$ kHz, and also determined the effective dipole-phonon coupling strength ($d_{	ext{PDM}}$).
method: The measurement relied on adiabatically ramping the motional trap frequency ($\omega_q$) while monitoring the resulting signal/null pattern across three overlapping frequency ranges, analyzed using advanced statistical methods like Hidden Markov Models (HMM).
model_or_system: The physical system is an ion chain ($	ext{CaO}^+$-$	ext{Ca}^+$) trapped in a linear trap. The underlying physics is modeled by an interaction Hamiltonian resembling the Jaynes-Cummings model, describing the coupling between the molecular dipole and the quantized motional phonon mode.
key_observables: The key observables are the signal/null pattern across three frequency ramps, the measured shelving probability ($p_s$), and the derived molecular splitting frequency ($\omega_{	ext{mol}}$).
important_parameters: The measured splitting is $\omega_{	ext{mol}} = 2\pi 	imes 454 \pm 1$ kHz, and the coupling strength was determined to be $d_{	ext{PDM}} = 2.56 \pm 0.07$ Debye.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian and relies on statistical modeling (HMM, Poisson likelihood) to distinguish true quantum signals from noise, while acknowledging limitations in coverage calibration.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the experimental setup, the energy level structure of $	ext{CaO}^+$, and the thermal population distribution of rotational states. Figure 2 details the procedure for the spectroscopic measurements.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup and theoretical model, describes the complex measurement protocol involving three frequency ramps and multiple diagnostic checks, presents the statistical analysis using HMMs to fit signal rates, and finally reports the derived spectroscopic constants.
why_interesting: This work is highly interesting as it pushes the boundaries of quantum sensing by applying a sophisticated quantum logic protocol (DPQL) to measure fundamental molecular properties ($\omega_{	ext{mol}}$) in a trapped-ion platform, bridging quantum optics, molecular physics, and quantum information.
